evidence: src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: `execute(state: any)` accepts an untyped raw input, not a typed application command or domain value.

src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: `if (Array.isArray(state)) { stateStr = state[0]?.toString() || ''; } else if (typeof state === 'string') { stateStr = state; }` normalizes the HTTP query-parameter shape (string | string[]), which is transport adapter logic (infrastructure).
src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: `this.orderRepository.findByState(stateStr as OrderStateType)` casts without validating against the domain state type.
Graph: OrderController (infrastructure) constructor-injects ListOrdersByStateUseCase, so the controller is the right place for request parsing.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The use case calls the repository port and maps results to an application DTO. Both fit the application layer. The problem is `execute(state: any)`. It checks `Array.isArray(state)`, takes `state[0]?.toString()`, falls back to `typeof state === 'string'`, and otherwise silently uses ''. This handles the shape of a raw HTTP query-string value: Express `req.query` can give a string, an array of strings or nothing. Parsing and normalizing transport input like this is the job of the transport/presentation adapter (here `OrderController` in infrastructure). An application use case should receive an already-validated `OrderStateType`. The unvalidated `stateStr as OrderStateType` cast also skips domain validation. Mapping to `OrderResponse` is acceptable work for the application layer. So the transport-parsing responsibility is in the wrong layer.

violations.message: The `execute` method parses raw HTTP query parameters (`Array.isArray(state)`, `state[0]?.toString()`, `typeof state === 'string'` on an `any` input). That is transport/presentation adapter work and belongs in infrastructure (e.g. OrderController). The use case should receive a validated OrderStateType.
